rule: A song is shown in the app only when its row is complete: every field below filled in, audioSource "generated", verifiedOn a date, and text and melody free (author dead for at least 70 full years, or for an anonymous work first published at least 70 full years ago). See KaraokeSongs.complete() in js/karaoke-songs.js. The rows are research by Claude and must be confirmed by LabLand before any commercial use.

songs.title: Au clair de la lune

songs.textVersion: Verses 1 and 2 as in Weckerlin, Chansons et rondes enfantines (Garnier, 1870), pp. 48-49 (scan on Wikisource); melody as in the same edition, transposed from G to C.

songs.textVersion: Weckerlin 1870 (p. 103): one verse, sung three times in unison (the source is a two-voice round; its short coda is left out). Wording of the source, including "Dig’, din, don".

songs.title: Jingle Bells

Pierpont's 1857 print ('The One Horse Open Sleigh', Oliver Ditson, Boston) differs slightly (e.g. 'o'er the hills', 'what joy it is to ride'); these small changes are anonymous folk variants of unknown date. The modern interjection 'hey!' is not sung (instrumental rest).

removed.title: Danny Boy
removed.reason: Licence OK but not included now. Frederic Weatherly wrote the words (1910, set to the Londonderry Air in 1913, Boosey & Co.) and died on 7 Sept 1929, so the text is free in the EU and UK (life + 70) and in the US (published 1913); the tune is traditional (Petrie, 1855). Not encoded because the Londonderry Air spans about an octave and a sixth, wider than the G3–D5 range used for older group voices, and a long rhythmically free melody that could not be checked note by note tonight. Can be added later in a lower key if LabLand wants it.

Deferred, not a licence problem.
